memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "But if, when the priest examines it, there is no white hair in it and it is not more than skin deep and has faded, then the priest is to isolate them for seven days. If it is spreading in the skin, the priest shall pronounce them unclean; it is a defiling disease. But if the spot is unchanged and has not spread, it is only a scar from the boil, and the priest shall pronounce them clean." - Lev 13:21-23 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here is the gentler outcome: it is only a scar from the boil.

A scar is not an active disease. It is the mark of something that has already been dealt with. It may be visible for life, but it is not spreading, and it does not make a person unclean.

Many believers cannot tell the difference between a scar and an open wound. We look at the evidence of our past — the marriage that ended, the years we wasted, the reputation that took a hit, the consequences we still live with — and we assume we are still unclean. We treat the scar as though it were an active infection.

But a scar is proof of healing, not of ongoing disease.

Think of it: the risen Christ kept His scars. He could have appeared in a flawless body, but He showed the marks in His hands and side (John 20:27). Those wounds were not evidence of defeat. They were the evidence of what He had accomplished.

Your history is not your condition. The consequences you carry are not the same thing as guilt before God. If Christ has dealt with it, what remains is a scar — and scars, in God's hands, become testimony.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Are you treating any healed area of your life as though it were still an open wound?
2. Can you tell the difference between consequence and condemnation?
3. How might God use your scars to help someone else?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that a scar is evidence of healing, not of ongoing disease. Help me to stop condemning myself for what You have already dealt with, and use my history for Your glory. Amen.
